standard_prerequisites.name: The transversal C and the equivalence relation on the reals
standard_prerequisites.statement: The relation on real numbers that makes r equivalent to s when r - s is rational is an equivalence relation, and C is a set selecting exactly one representative from each equivalence class.
standard_prerequisites.use: The defining property of C is used at source lines 1031-1032 to pass from r_1 equivalent to r_2 to r_1 = r_2.

standard_prerequisites.name: The group of rational rotations
standard_prerequisites.statement: The set of maps rho_r : x maps to x + r for rational r, with composition and inversion, is a group that preserves the equivalence relation.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof forms the composite of rho_1 with the inverse of rho_2 and observes that it lies in the group (source lines 1029-1031), which is what turns the two representations of s into an equivalence between r_1 and r_2.

core_obligations: Assume a common point s of the two images and unfold the two representations s = rho_1(r_1) = rho_2(r_2) with r_1, r_2 in C (source lines 1027-1028).

Apply the inverse of rho_2 to both sides to obtain that rho_1 followed by the inverse of rho_2, which is a rational rotation, maps r_1 to r_2; conclude that r_1 and r_2 are equivalent (source lines 1029-1031).

Use that C selects exactly one member of each equivalence class to get r_1 = r_2, then s = rho_1(r_1) = rho_2(r_1), and finally that two rational rotations agreeing at one point coincide, i.e. rho_1 = rho_2, contradicting the hypothesis (source lines 1031-1033).

proof_roadmap.step: Take a point in the intersection and write it as rho_1(r_1) = r_2(r_2) with representatives in C.
Compose with the inverse of rho_2 to exhibit a rational rotation carrying r_1 to r_2, hence an equivalence.
Use the one-representative-per-class property of C to get r_1 = r_2 and hence rho_1 = rho_2, so the intersection is empty.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma vitalinooverlap at source lines 1022-1024: if the two rational shifts rho_1 and rho_2 are distinct, then the images of the transversal C under them are disjoint. The proof at source lines 1026-1034 is the paving step of the Vitali construction and has to chain four separate facts: a common point s of the two images gives representations s = rho_1(r_1) = rho_2(r_2) with r_1, r_2 in C; from that one must manipulate the shifts to exhibit the composite rho_1 composed with the inverse of rho_2 as an element of the group of rational rotations; one must know that the group elements preserve the equivalence relation, so r_1 and r_2 are equivalent; and one must use the defining property of the transversal C, that it selects exactly one member from each equivalence class, to conclude r_1 = r_2 and hence s = rho_1(r_1) = rho_2(r_1), whence rho_1 = rho_2. Nothing in the statement records which of these steps is needed, and the cancellation of the shifts is the non-obvious move. No result outside the retained text is used.

compared.difference: rotationsgroupabelian (statement 936-938, proof 940-956) counts the group-theoretic fact that the rational rotations commute. Our candidate is the disjointness lemma about the transversal and only uses that the rotations form a group, not that they commute.

vitalicover (statement 1012-1014, proof 1016-1020) covers the reals by the images of C; our candidate proves that the pieces of that cover are pairwise disjoint, which is the complementary half of the paving argument.
